payload.task_text:
Our team uses a popular tech education channel for ongoing developer learning. I need a monthly digest of content published in the first half of 2025 to help our team stay current on trending tech topics.

From our video database, retrieve all videos from the Fireship channel published between January 2025 and June 2025 inclusive. For each calendar month in that range, identify the single top video by view count.

Create a presentation file called Fireship_2025_Digest.pptx in your workspace. The presentation must have a title slide with the exact title text "Fireship 2025 Monthly Tech Digest" and then one content slide for each of the six months (January through June 2025), for a total of seven slides. Each monthly slide must use the month and year as the slide title (for example "January 2025"). The body content of each monthly slide must include all four of the following pieces of information: the top video title for that month, the view count formatted as a plain integer, the video duration converted to minutes and rounded to one decimal place, and the total count of videos published by the channel in that month.

Schedule a monthly review meeting in the shared calendar for each of the six months. Use these exact dates and times: 2025-01-07 from 09:00 to 09:30, 2025-02-04 from 09:00 to 09:30, 2025-03-04 from 09:00 to 09:30, 2025-04-01 from 09:00 to 09:30, 2025-05-06 from 09:00 to 09:30, and 2025-06-03 from 09:00 to 09:30. Use the America/New_York timezone for all calendar events in this task. Each event title must follow the exact pattern "Monthly Tech Digest Review - [Month Year]" where Month Year is the full month name and year such as "January 2025". Each event description must mention the title of the top video for that month.

Send an email to team@company.com with the subject line "Fireship 2025 Monthly Digest Ready". The email body must list all six monthly top videos, each including the video title and its view count. Ensure all six months from January through June 2025 are represented in the email body.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use one wave with exactly one Coder sub-agent. That agent should keep the complete channel scan, six monthly selections, and presentation together; a separate source wave would add a redundant handoff.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 1 Coder sub-agent:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Use one Coder sub-agent to own one complete read-only Fireship channel catalog session and `Fireship_2025_Digest.pptx`. Obtain one channel list identifier, navigate the returned list identifier sequentially at the maximum supported page size until an empty page or source exhaustion, and preserve Video_ID, full title, published timestamp, integer view count, and duration. Filter locally to January 1 through June 30, 2025 inclusive. For each of the six calendar months, count all candidates and choose the single highest-view video with a stable Video_ID tie-break; report a source-empty month rather than inventing one. Convert duration to minutes once. Create one presentation identifier and exactly seven slides: the exact title plus six chronological month slides, each containing all four required values. Read the deck back and return path, compact six-month table, channel page/row/date/ranking controls, and slide count/content checks.

After Wave 1, the main agent validates all six selections, then issues six `list_events` calls natively in parallel using narrow ISO ranges around the original slots and sufficient `maxResults`; inspect exact title/time locally. Issue only missing `create_event` calls natively in parallel with exact `start.dateTime`/`end.dateTime`, `timeZone="America/New_York"` in both objects, exact titles, and that month's verified top-video title in its description. Retrieve each returned/reused ID with `get_event`. Only after deck and event inventory agree, check Sent mail and send one missing exact-recipient/subject email listing all six month/title/integer-view pairs. Read it back and finish without another wave.

nodes.text:
You are building the data + presentation half of a monthly digest task. Work ONLY inside your task-scoped workspace and with the granted MCP tools (YouTube MCP, PPTX MCP, filesystem MCP, local python). Do NOT touch the calendar or email tools — the parent agent handles those.

GOAL
1) Scan the ENTIRE catalog of the Fireship YouTube channel (the popular tech education channel). Find the channel via YouTube search if needed (e.g. mcp__youtube__videos_searchVideos with query "Fireship", then read the channelId from results; or any available channel-lookup path). 
2) Obtain ONE channel videos list session via mcp__youtube__channels_listVideos (channelId, maxResults=20, sortOrder="newest"). Then navigate that list session sequentially with mcp__youtube__channels_navigateList (page numbers 1, 2, 3, ...) until an empty page or source exhaustion. For EVERY video in every page, capture: Video_ID, full title, published timestamp, and (via mcp__youtube__videos_getVideo with parts including snippet/statistics/contentDetails for each video) the integer view count and ISO-8601 duration (e.g. PT12M34S). Preserve ALL videos — do not stop early.
3) Filter locally to videos published between 2025-01-01T00:00:00 and 2025-06-30T23:59:59 inclusive (compare against the published timestamp).
4) For EACH calendar month January through June 2025: (a) count ALL videos published in that month (this is the "total count of videos published by the channel in that month"), (b) pick the single highest-view video. Tie-break ONLY if two videos in the same month have exactly equal view counts: choose the lexicographically smallest Video_ID. If a month has zero videos, report it as source-empty explicitly — do NOT invent data.
5) Convert each duration to minutes: parse ISO-8601 duration (PT#H#M#S) into total seconds, divide by 60, round to ONE decimal place. The view count stays a plain integer.
6) Create the presentation: use mcp__pptx__create_presentation to get a presentation ID. Build exactly SEVEN slides in order:
   - Slide 1 (title slide): exact title text "Fireship 2025 Monthly Tech Digest" (use a title-slide layout; set the title exactly).
   - Slides 2-7 (one per month, chronological): each slide's TITLE must be exactly the month and year, e.g. "January 2025", "February 2025", ..., "June 2025". Each monthly slide's BODY must include ALL FOUR of these pieces of information: (i) the top video title for that month, (ii) the view count formatted as a plain integer, (iii) the video duration in minutes rounded to one decimal place, (iv) the total count of videos published by the channel in that month. Format the body so all four values are clearly present and readable (e.g. labeled lines).
7) Save the deck to the absolute path: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-yt-fireship-ppt-gcal-email/workspace/Fireship_2025_Digest.pptx (use mcp__pptx__save_presentation with that file_path).
8) Verify by reading the deck back with mcp__pptx__extract_presentation_text: confirm exactly 7 slides, slide 1 title is exactly "Fireship 2025 Monthly Tech Digest", and each month slide has the correct month title and contains its four required values.

RETURN (as your final report — be precise and complete):
- Absolute path of the saved .pptx file.
- A compact six-month table with columns: Month (e.g. "2025-01"), top_video_title, view_count (plain integer), duration_minutes (rounded to 1 decimal), total_videos_in_month. Include it for all six months, or explicitly flag any month as source-empty.
- Channel list session ID, the page numbers scanned, row indices, and any ranking/ordering controls you used (so the parent can audit).
- Verification results: slide count, each slide's title, and confirmation each monthly body contains its four values.
- The exact Video_ID of each month's top video.

Constraints: use max page size (20). Do not skip pages. Do not fabricate any video, view count, duration, or count. If the YouTube API returns fewer/more pages than expected, report exactly what you observed.
Fireship channel scan + pptx build
